What drives housing prices in the Lille metropolitan area?

Public property sales (DVF), 2021-2025

Maureen Wiart

October 2026

The question

Buyers, lenders and estate agents all ask the same thing: is this price in line with the market? This report uses every recorded sale of a flat or a house in the 95 communes of the Métropole Européenne de Lille between 2021 and 2025 to answer three questions:

  1. How have prices moved since 2021, once differences in the homes sold are taken into account?
  2. How much does location matter?
  3. How well can a home’s price be estimated from public data, and which sales stand out?

Data. Demandes de valeurs foncières géolocalisées (DVF), published by Etalab from the tax administration’s records, open licence. One row per item of a sale; a sale with a flat, a cellar and a parking space appears three times with the same total price. To get a reliable price per m², the analysis keeps sales of exactly one dwelling (with or without outbuildings) and removes implausible values.

Step Rows
Rows in the Nord files, 2021-2025 553,756
Sale rows in the 95 MEL communes 211,037
Sales of exactly one dwelling 76,689
After quality filters (surface, price, price per m²) 76,047

1. Prices since 2021

Median prices per m² barely move: flats went from 3,131 € in 2021 to 3,084 € in 2025. But medians can mislead: when interest rates rose in 2023, fewer first-time buyers bought small flats, so the mix of homes sold changed.

A quality-adjusted index separates the two effects. A regression explains the log of the price per m² by the commune, the type of home, its surface and number of rooms, and one coefficient per year: that coefficient is the price change for a comparable home.

Year Quality-adjusted index Raw median index
2021 100.0 100.0
2022 104.6 104.8
2023 101.9 103.5
2024 98.1 99.0
2025 100.4 101.2

Comparable homes gained about 5% in 2022, then lost about 6% by 2024 as rates rose, before recovering in 2025 to roughly their 2021 level. The raw median overstates 2023: the homes sold that year were, on average, more expensive kinds of homes.

2. Location

A square metre costs more than twice as much in Marcq-en-Barœul or Lille as in Roubaix or Tourcoing, a few kilometres away. The map shows the gradient: the centre of Lille and the north-western suburbs on one side, the north-eastern former textile towns on the other.

3. Estimating a price

The valuation model explains the log of the price by the log of the surface (with a different slope for houses), the number of rooms, the commune and the quarter of the sale. It was fitted on 80% of the sales and tested on the other 20%.

Measure Value
Share of price variation explained (R², training) 0.632
Sales in the test set 15,292
Median error on test sales 20.8%
Test sales within ±20% of the estimate 48.5%
Sold more than 50% above the estimate 8.7%
Sold more than 50% below the estimate 3.2%

A typical error of about ±21% is honest for public data: DVF says nothing about a home’s condition, floor, view, energy rating or renovation. The model is good enough to screen sales, not to value one specific home.

What it says about a 60 m², 3-room flat sold at the end of 2025:

Commune Estimated price
Lille 196,000 €
Roubaix 95,000 €
Marcq-en-Barœul 224,000 €
Villeneuve-d’Ascq 181,000 €

What this means in practice

  • For a buyer or a lender: prices for comparable homes are back to their 2021 level after the 2022-2024 correction; a price well above the model’s range deserves a closer look at what justifies it.
  • For a bank checking collateral: an automatic estimate can flag mortgage files where the purchase price is far above the market (about 8.7% of sales are more than 50% above the estimate) and send only those to a full appraisal.
  • For compliance teams: a property bought far above or below its market value is a classic red flag for money laundering in real estate. A screen like this one is a cheap first filter, to combine with the other indicators.

Limits: no information on condition or energy rating; the 20% test sample is random, not later in time; outliers are removed with simple bounds. The full code is in the R/ folder of the project.
